new_statements.quote: Akzente sind nur gesetzt, wenn in mehrsilbigen Wörtern der Druck auf einer anderen als auf der vorletzten Silbe ruht.
new_statements.translation: Accents are only written when, in polysyllabic words, the stress rests on a syllable other than the penultimate one.
new_statements.citation: Peekel, Gerhard. 1929-30. Grammatische Grundzüge und Wörterverzeichnis der Label-Sprache im Süden von Neu-Mecklenburg. Zeitschrift für Eingeborenen-Sprachen 20 (Heft 1-2): 10-34, 92-120 (Hamburg/Berlin: Reimer).
new_statements.locator: p. 13, Part I 'Grammatische Grundzüge der Label-Sprache', section 'Lautsystem und Schreibung', final paragraph (immediately before 'Der Artikel'); volume page scan PA13 of Google Books id Qow2X63r7zYC (= HathiTrust mdp.39015035866451)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls by default on the penultimate syllable; words whose stress falls elsewhere are lexically marked with an acute accent in Peekel's transcription (examples on the same page: labúr 'strong', lamás 'coconut', kiár 'rain' -- final stress).
new_statements.exceptions: Yes: non-penultimate stress exists in a minority of polysyllabic words and is flagged orthographically with an acute (labúr, lamás, kiár on p. 13; the Wörterverzeichnis pp. 92-120, not obtained, presumably marks further cases). Breve/macron marks on vowels (mŭtmut, gĕnĕs, kŏk) indicate length, not stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('in mehrsilbigen Wörtern'); the statement is an orthographic convention in the sound-system section of a sketch built from 1909-10 notes taken at Namatanai from two Kait-born police soldiers (Vorwort, p. 10); Peekel himself warns the material is small and not error-free (p. 11). No information on phrase-level accent or citation forms.
new_statements.identity_note: Peekel's 'Label-Sprache im Süden von Neu-Mecklenburg' is labe1239 Label [lbb]: Ross 1988:257 identifies it as the language of Nasko (southernmost west-coast village of southern New Ireland), a few old speakers at Kait, and Tampakar; Peekel's data were dictated 1909-10 at Namatanai by two police soldiers from Kait (p. 10). Not to be confused with Kandas [kqw] (Watpi, King, Kait), a distinct language closely related to Duke of York; Lithgow & Claassen 1968 mislabelled Peekel's Label vocabulary as 'Kandas'. 'Lambel/Lambell' in Stephan & Graebner 1907 and Capell 1971 is the regional name (coast from Cape St George to Laur).

Only vol. pp. 9-13 (article pp. 10-13: Vorwort, Abkürzungen, map, sound system, start of 'Der Artikel') could be pulled from the Google Books full-view copy (id Qow2X63r7zYC, Univ. of Michigan; = HathiTrust mdp.39015035866451, rights pdus/Full view) before Google blocke…

sources.note: Bibliography only: Peekel 1929-30 is the sole descriptive source; the other two Glottolog refs (Ramscar et al. 2010, Moreau et al. 2018) are false hits on the word 'label'.

sources.citation: Stephan, Emil & Fritz Graebner. 1907. Neu-Mecklenburg (Bismarck-Archipel): die Küste von Umuddu bis Kap St. Georg. Berlin: Reimer. (Glottolog's second 'med' for labe1239: wordlist)
sources.note: Chapter 'Sprache' (p. 138 ff.) is a general essay on Melanesian grammar and elicitation problems; wordlists p. 219 ff. (Laur, Lambell, King). No hit for Betonung/Akzent/betont; scanned text carries no accent marks.
No phonology; records that a Label New Testament (Wycliffe Bible Translators Australia, © 2023, launched 24 Nov 2024) required creating an alphabet; eBible.org confirms the NT (lbb, WBT Australia).

sources.note: Only mentions Peekel (1909, 1930) as descriptions of Patpatar and 'Kandas' (=Label) and Label's a/na article allomorphy (p. 70); no Label stress information; no Label sketch in the volume.

sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Label appears only in cognate sets and sound-correspondence tables (Peekel's data). No stress statement for Label. Identity passage p. 257: Lithgow & Claassen's (1968) 'Kandas' vocabulary is actually Peekel's Label; Peekel's Label is spoken at Nasko, by a few old people at Kait, and at Tampakar; Kandas (Watpi, King, Kait) is a distinct language. p. 261 lists Peekel 1929-30 as the description of Label.

sources.citation: Beaumont, Clive H. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Ireland. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study vol. 2 (Pacific Linguistics C-39), 387-397.
sources.note: Phonology treated only as historical sound changes for subgrouping (reflexes of *p, syllable loss); Kandas in the wordlist table; no mention of stress or accent for any language.

sources.citation: Beaumont, Clive H. 1972. New Ireland languages: a review. Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 3 (Pacific Linguistics A-35), 1-41.
sources.note: §1.4 Phonology (pp. 21-22) is a phonetic survey of all New Ireland languages (stops, fricatives, nasals, vowels, tone in Kara/Barok); nothing on stress in Label/Kandas; only remark on stress is that the author's own 1969 Tigak stress conclusions need revision. Lists Peekel 1929-30 in the bibliography; Table 1 notes Capell's list has 'Lambel'.
